sources.description: Katanasound Venomous Snake: Unleash the Venom: Katanasound's Venomous Snake Octave Fuzz Channeling the iconic Octavia fuzz of yesteryear, the Venomous Snake from Katanasound delivers…
sources.snippet: Katanasound Venomous Snake - Multi-Effects Pedal | PedalFinder
sources.bodyExcerpt: Katanasound Venomous Snake - Multi-Effects Pedal | PedalFinder Guitar Pedal Finder Explore Brands Guides Pedalboards FAQ Home / Katanasound / Venomous Snake Katanasound Venomous Snake Unleash the Venom: Katanasound's Venomous Snake Octave Fuzz Channeling the iconic Octavia fuzz of yesteryear, the Venomous Snake from Katanasound delivers a truly venomous tone. This pedal's custom-designed circuitry captures the essence of that legendary Tychobrahe sound, but with a modern twist that makes it truly bite. Crank the Mix knob, and you'll be rewarded with a snarling, metallic fuzz tone that leaps an entire octave above your original signal. The result is a bold, aggressive sound that's perfect for searing lead lines, thunderous riffs, and mind-bending sonic explorations. But don't let the Venomous Snake's ferocity fool you – this pedal also provides just the right amount of natural compression and a smooth, responsive release, ensuring your tone remains tight and focused. Dial the Mix knob back, and the Venomous Snake transforms into a more traditional fuzz, retaining that signature Katanasound character but with a thicker, more distorted edge. It's a versatile pedal that can tackle everything from classic rock crunch to modern metal mayhem, all while injecting your sound with a touch of reptilian venom. Whether you're chasing the holy grail of octave fuzz or simply seeking a new and inspiring way to sculpt your guitar tone, the Venomous Snake from Katanasound is a must-have addition to any discerning player's pedalboard. Prepare to be bitten by the snake's irresistible allure. Katanasound Venomous Snake Octave Fuzz Pedal - Gbase Gbase - Guitars Amps More Gear Dealers Radar Events More Sections Gear Dealers Events Blog Account Join Login Create Store Help 1.0.731 Home Find Gear Find Dealer Gear Radar Events Blog Join Login Create Store Help Find Gear Effects Katanasound Venomous Snake Octave Fuzz Pedal Andy Babiuk's Fab Gear Description NEW - Inspired by the sound of Tychobrahe's "Octavia," the original circuitry I developed for Venomous Snake provides an extremely bright and metallic sound. The violent and unique sound still gives just the right amount of compression and a natural release level, making Venomous Snake one of my proudest creations. The Mix dial controls the Octave ratio, and turning to 3 o'clock gives the Octavia-like sound. Turning the mix to the left lowers the Octave ratio, giving a bold fuzz sound. IN STOCK AND READY TO SHIP! About Katanasound At Fab Gear we stock the full line of hand made Katanasound effects pedals because they just kick ass!!! Mitch makes some of the finest sounding, most durable pedals available. If you want a cool sounding old pedal but your worried if it's going to crap out live on stage and make you look stupid, then you need a Katanasound pedal. It's the sound you love from an old pedal but built like a tank!! For years in The Chesterfield Kings we have always tried to use old effect pedals live but they would always crap out and get wrecked. Now we've been trashing Katanasound pedals live on stage and they just keep working and sounding great!! They never fail!! A note about Katanasound from its founder... In the 1990s, many Japanese looking for top sounding products purchased expensive, vintage pedals imported from the West. While sounding amazing, the circuitry was often overcomplicated, with soldering of poor quality. As a result, few could tolerate the rigors of intense use. Many in the industry asked me to repair these vintage pedals, providing a chance to study their strengths - as well as their weaknesses. I combine the excellent sound of the Western products with the diligence and detail of Japan into durable, top-quality pedals that best serve today's serious guitarists. My pedals show their uniqueness from the first test riff, and I back up the rich sound with high-quality craftsmanship and parts. I try to add a jolt of individuality and a soul that strikes to the heart. Many people are surprised by the low noise level, but there is no secret to this. Simple circuitry with proper board design, quality craftsmanship and no extra wiring minimizes noise while providing the best response and rich overtones. These products are by no means cheap. Unlike others who use cheap parts and/or labor to save on costs, I am committed to personally producing the best hand-made quality, and I use the parts necessary for this. These pedals are designed for serious musicians, and are well regarded in the Japanese industry by pro musicians as well as those who think of the guitar as more than a "hobby." sources.title: Keeley Electronics 1962 British Overdrive - Pedal of the Day
sources.description: The Keeley Electronics 1962 British Overdrive defines early classic amplifier tones - heavy, cutting, the very definition of classic British Overdrive.
sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics 1962 British Overdrive - Pedal of the Day
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics 1962 British Overdrive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Keeley Electronics 1962 British Overdrive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Sunday, August 16, 2015 in Keeley Electronics, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> I want to just say right up front that this pedal from Keeley Electronics oozes quality. It just pours out of it. It’s solid, well bit and the finish is flawless. Very understated and clean looking. You can tell right away that it’s not an imported piece of tin. Built solid and to last.The simple gold stripe with the 1962 off to the side is a very classy way to say it’s what’s on the inside that counts. Now the fun part. I play at home for me, my dog Sparkey and occasionally the cat. Doodles. I mostly play through small, one to five watt tube combos. I love the Blackstar HT1-R and the Vox AC4TV. My main amp for my pedal board is an Orange Micro Terror and 8″ speaker cab. I’d love to get the sound of a Marshall stack or a Bluesbreaker but I know it’s not possible with my gear. I can come close. But not exactly there. Until now. I don’t know how the masterminds at Keeley & Co. do it, but every pedal I’ve tried of theirs has been a wonder. This one is no exception. Out of the velvet like bag it came in, plugged into the board we were off. With a few adjustments I went from a singing, soaring lead tone, with what seemed like sustain for days, to a Cream-y, Green-y crunch. After a while spent trying different settings, I settled into one that had me playing A Whole Lotta Love, for a whole lotta time. I’m going to miss that EHX Soul Food, but it’s spot has been taken. Permanently. You’ve got to try it to believe it . If the 1962 British Overdrive makes my little rig sound this good, I can only imagine what it could do…… Submitted by Mike F, Instagram , Twitter GET EXCLUSIVE UPDATES, CONTEST INFO, SEE OUR LATEST DEMO VIDEOS AND MORE: More info at: Submit a Comment Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. Here at Keeley we are not one to sit on a circuit, we constantly dream and imagine what else it could be. So we have come up with something more for the Keeley 1962, Introducing the 1962x. The 1962x is a limited version of our 1962, built in batches when we have the supply, with an additional “KT88” high headroom mode utilizing MOSFET clipping. In the “KT66” mode you will get the same performance and gain range you get in the standard 1962, from mild light breakup all the way to full saturation. In the “KT88” mode, a MOSFET transistor is inserted in the clipping stage to produce a higher output, and a more forceful, focused and meatier sound. The KT88 Mode definitely steps the presence up a notch and acts terrifically to light up the front end of a classic tube amp (maybe even a Bluesbreaker?). Take all of this and place it in a brand new graphic design featuring many classic Bluesbreaker design elements and a special printed “open back” back plate, and you end up with a terrific sounding pedal, that is really great to look at too! sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics 1962x 2-Mode Limited British Overdrive
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics 1962x Limited British Overdrive - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Keeley Electronics 1962x 2-Mode Limited British Overdrive Posted By Pedal of the Day on Saturday, July 20, 2019 in Keeley Electronics, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> There’s no shortage of amazing effects coming out of the Keeley Electronics camp, as they have been for close to 2 decades now, and we always love it when something new comes through the office. While the past couple of years have seen bigger, more option-filled pedals like the Dark Side , Aria , Super Mod Workstation and more, sometimes you just need a killer overdrive pedal to get you in the right mood, and spark some creativity in your playing. The 1962x is a British overdrive pedal that gives you some classic Bluesbreaker-type tones, crafted using precision components and only the finest workmanship, as you’d of course expect from Robert and his team…. Gain, Treble and Boost make up the simple control section on the 1962x , leading to a wide range of British black-and-gold amplifier sounds throughout the spectrum of these parameters. There’s more to this pedal, however, in the form of a teeny, tiny toggle switch. Select KT88 to enter into a high headroom boost mode, or go with KT66 for your standard overdrive sound. The circuit has been wrapped in Keeley’s own Katana Boost, creating preamp and output tube distortion characteristics with ease. The KT88 mode inserts a MOSFET transistor into the clipping stage, making an already powerful drive tone beefed up, for higher output and a meatier overall sound. The 1962x also plays great with others, especially Klons (or Klones , if you’re like most players), creating fat, rich lead tones for days. Tons of sustain here, coupled with a killer graphic to emulate some vintage amps to add to the nostalgia and force of this absolute beast of a drive. A real amp in a box effect, this one will put a smile on your face the moment you engage it, and for years to come afterwards. Cheers once again to Robert and the entire Keeley Electronics staff, for crushing it AGAIN (we never get tired of saying that) – check out our demo for a taste of what the 1962x is capable of, and then head over to the Keeley site to try and grab one for yourself (if they’re in stock). sources.description: The Keeley Angry Orange is a versatile 4-in-1 guitar effects pedal, offering a blend of classic fuzz and distortion tones. This pedal combines a '78 Japanese distortion and a '91 Soviet fuzz circuit to create both familiar and unique sounds. Guitarists can explore new hybrid fuzz and distortion tones with the intuitive three-knob control and switch between buffered and true bypass modes for flexible signal chain setups. The all-analog circuit delivers saturated tones suitable for professional use and is manufactured in the USA. This pedal also won the Premier Guitar's Premier Gear Award!

The Keeley Angry Orange is a 4-in-1 pedal that gives you two well-known fuzz and distortion circuits and allows you to create two dope new hybrid tones! It’s sort of like pedal-modeling except these are 100% old-school, analog circuits and you decide which tone control or clipping section you want to rock. Heavily saturate your guitar through either a legendary ‘78 Japanese Orange Distortion or a ‘91 Soviet Civil War Fuzz. Use the Angry Orange to make your own fuzzztortions with the hybrid modes, all with only three simple knobs. This pedal can be True Bypass or Buffered Bypass, it only takes two seconds to switch between the modes. The Keeley Angry Orange is entirely manufactured at Keeley Electronics and is in our new aluminum enclosure. $199 Made In The USA. Tone Control The Angry Orange gives you two tone control circuits to choose from. When the Tone Switch is up and in the MF Position the tone control is a scooped sounding, passive tilt-style. If the Tone Switch is down and in the DS Position it also features a passive sounding tilt control, voiced a little differently. Diode Clipping Hard or Soft Clipping: The Angry Orange gives you both styles of diode clipping. Diodes are used to create hard clipping distortions or smooth overdrive sounds. If the Clipping Switch is in the DS Position it features Hard Diode Clipping which is an edgier, more aggressive tone. When the Clipping Switch is in the MF Position that uses Soft Diode Clipping, like a muffled fuzz tone. Angry Orange – Buffered Bypass or True Bypass The Keeley Electronics Angry Orange Distortion and Fuzz features our Jfet buffer for noise free switching. We developed an amazing sounding buffer which not only makes your rig sound better, it gives you silent switching with no tone loss. No more pops and clicks to distract from your music. If you want to turn that feature off and go back to true bypass, simply press and hold down the foot switch for two seconds and the pedal will switch to True-Bypass (LED will flash twice). True Bypass is great for players that want the effect of plugging directly into their amp when the pedal is off. The Blues Disorder has two switches that allow you to separate the tone control from the clipping section. By mixing and matching the Tone and Drive switches you get two hybrid sounds.…
sources.snippet: Keeley Blues Disorder Overdrive And Distortion
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Blues Disorder Overdrive And Distortion - Built for Tone, Playability and Performance Across Electric, Acoustic and Bass Guitars Welcome to Our Store My account Contact Us Cart Checkout Home Best Value Acoustic Guitars Electric Guitars Bass Guitars Amplifiers View All Home / Effects / Keeley Blues Disorder Overdrive And Distortion Keeley Blues Disorder Overdrive And Distortion In stock Keeley Electronics Blues Disorder Overdrive and DistortionKeeley combines two completely different overdrive and distortion circuits to create four different drives in one box. The Blues Disorder has two switches that allow you to separate the tone control $ 199.00 $ 99.50 Add to cart Category: Effects Share : Description Reviews (0) Keeley Electronics Blues Disorder Overdrive and Distortion Keeley combines two completely different overdrive and distortion circuits to create four different drives in one box. The Blues Disorder has two switches that allow you to separate the tone control from the clipping section. By mixing and matching the Tone and Drive switches you get two hybrid sounds. With both switches up its a smooth, soft-clipping Bluesy Breaker. The BB side is a low gain, soft-clipping overdrive. With both switches down its a fuller sounding, hard-clipping OC Distortion. The clever design keeps the pedal a simple three knob overdrive with 4 unique sounds. Switch easily between buffered or true-bypass; whichever sounds best in your rig. The Keeley Blues Disorder Overdrive and Distortion is designed and manufactured entirely by Keeley Electronics in our brand new aluminum enclosure. The Blues Disorder is two complete analog drive circuits. It has both a hard-clipping distortion and a soft clipping overdrive Toggle between tone stacks or gain stages. Create hybrid overdrives by swapping Drive and Tone circuits. True Bypass or Buffered Bypass Use the buffer to improve your rigs tone. Switch to true bypass in two seconds. Simply hold the stomp switch down to switch anytime. Keeley pedals are engineered in our tone lab and sonically perfected with the help of studio and touring musicians. These instruments are built entirely in our factory. SWITCHABLE TONE STACKS SWAP VOICINGS The Blues Disorder gives you two tone control circuits to choose from. When the Tone Switch is down and in the OC position you will hear an active midrange boost and then the tone control rolls off high-frequency. If the Tone Switch is up and in the BB position you dont have the active mid-boost, theres just a simple high-frequency filter and therefore a more transparent sounding overdrive and response. SWITCHABLE DIODES HYBRID GAIN The Blues Disorder gives you both styles of diode clipping. Where diodes are placed in the circuit, can have a dramatic effect on gain and compression. This pedal gives you both hard clipping distortion or soft clipping overdrive, depending on the position of the Drive Toggle. If the Clipping Switch is in the OC position it features Hard-Clipping which is an edgier, more aggressive tone. Alternatively, when the Clipping Switch is in the BB Position, that uses Soft-Clipping and sounds like a softly overdriven tube amplifier. BUFFERED BYPASS OR TRUE BYPASS The Keeley Blues Disorder allows you to quickly switch between either mode. Having a great buffer will make your rig sound strong and clear even when the pedal is off. Buffered switching prevents the pops and clicks of true-bypass switching. If you want to turn on true-bypass, simply press and hold the foot switch for two seconds. Holding the switch for two seconds toggle between modes. True Bypass is great if a buffer might affect the tone of a vintage pedal. Enjoy truly silent switching and a better sounding rig with Keeleys buffered switching mode. Reviews There are no reviews yet. sources.description: A detailed, educator-led examination of Keeley Electronics’ 2024 flagship pedal — its dual analog delay engines, true-stereo reverb architecture, component-level design choices, and practical implications for guitar pedagogy, live performance, and studio workflow.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Unveils The Dark Side: A Deep Technical and Pedagogical Analysis of the New Dual-Engine Analog Delay/Reverb Pedal | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / practice tips practice tips Keeley Electronics Unveils The Dark Side: A Deep Technical and Pedagogical Analysis of the New Dual-Engine Analog Delay/Reverb Pedal By Nina Harper July 22, 2026 What Is The Dark Side — And Why It Matters to Guitar Educators Keeley Electronics’ The Dark Side , unveiled in March 2024 at the NAMM Show in Anaheim, is not just another multi-effect pedal — it’s a paradigm shift in analog-digital hybrid signal processing. Designed by Robert Keeley and engineered by lead designer Chris Riddle, this 100% hand-wired, USA-built unit integrates two independent analog BBD (Bucket Brigade Device) delay lines — one using MN3207 chips (128-stage), the other MN3007 (512-stage) — alongside a fully discrete, 24-bit/96kHz stereo reverb engine powered by the Bela Platform FPGA. With 1200ms max analog delay time (dual-path sum), true-stereo I/O, MIDI over USB-C and TRS, and an onboard expression pedal input with assignable parameters, The Dark Side bridges vintage warmth with modern precision. For music educators, its programmable presets, consistent latency ( Inside the Dual Analog Delay Architecture The heart of The Dark Side lies in its two separate analog delay circuits — a deliberate departure from single-engine designs common in pedals like the Strymon El Capistan or Boss DD-8. Each delay path features its own dedicated MN3207 (Path A) and MN3007 (Path B) BBD chips, both operating at ±15V rails for extended headroom and reduced noise floor (measured at -89.4dBu A-weighted, per Audio Precision APx555 bench tests). Unlike many analog delays that use clock dividers or digital tap control, Keeley retains fully analog clock generation via discrete JFET-based oscillators — delivering temperature-stable timing within ±0.3% across 0–40°C ambient ranges. Signal Path Integrity and Component Choices Every audio path in The Dark Side uses 1% metal-film resistors and Wima FKP2 polypropylene film capacitors — components selected for low dielectric absorption and minimal phase shift. The MN3207 path delivers 20–600ms of warm, slightly compressed delay with natural high-end roll-off (−3dB at 4.8kHz), while the MN3007 path extends cleanly to 1200ms with tighter low-end response (−3dB at 75Hz) and improved transient preservation. Crucially, both paths feature independent feedback loops with buffered op-amp summing stages (Texas Instruments OPA2134) to prevent cascade-induced oscillation — a known issue in older dual-BBD units like the Electro-Harmonix Memory Man Stereo. Real-Time Parameter Interaction Each delay path offers dedicated Time, Regen (feedback), Mix, and Tone controls — but what sets The Dark Side apart is its Sync Mode . When engaged, the Time knobs lock to internal tempo divisions (1/4, 1/8T, 1/4T, dotted 1/4) with sub-division accuracy of ±0.7ms. This enables precise rhythmic layering without external tap tempo — vital for student exercises in metric modulation and polyrhythmic phrasing. Additionally, holding the Preset button for 1.5 seconds activates Time Shift , which offsets Path B’s delay time by ±120ms relative to Path A — creating lush chorusing or slapback-to-sustain textures in real time. The Discrete Stereo Reverb Engine While many boutique reverb pedals rely on digital DSP chips (e.g., the Eventide H9’s SHARC processor or the Walrus Audio Mako R1’s ARM Cortex-M4), Keeley opted for a hybrid approach: a custom-designed, FPGA-based reverb core built on the open-source Bela Platform. This allows for sample-accurate convolution and algorithmic modeling without proprietary lock-in. The reverb engine runs at 24-bit/96kHz with 512MB of onboard DDR3 RAM for impulse response storage — enabling up to eight user-loaded IRs (each up to 8 seconds long at 96kHz) alongside four factory algorithms: Hall , Plate , Sprin

Keeley Electronics browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Keeley ALS Drive For A Cure Published on February 6, 2019 Keeley Electronics overdrive pedal Information Keeley Electronics The Drive for a Cure is a limited edition overdrive pedal collaboratively designed by Keeley Electronics and Peter Gusmano for the Guitar for a Cure initiative, created to support ALS research through Project ALS. Only 50 units were produced, each individually numbered and signed, with $30 from each sale donated to the charity. The pedal features a unique Symmetry Switch for selecting between symmetrical and asymmetrical clipping modes. In the left position, the clipping is symmetrical, producing a slightly higher gain with lower output volume. In the right position, asymmetrical clipping delivers a more tube-like response with slightly less gain but increased output volume. The tone control circuit is modified to reduce less high frequency content than typical designs, resulting in a brighter, more lively sound. This boutique pedal was packaged with special items acknowledging the cause and was sold at a lower price point than other Keeley models to encourage broad support. Controls Symmetry Switch (Gain Switch): Selects symmetrical (more gain, less volume) or asymmetrical (less gain, more volume, tube-like feel) clipping Tone: Modified to retain more high frequencies for increased brilliance Gain: Adjusts the amount of overdrive Volume: Sets the overall output level Highlights Limited run of 50 units, numbered and signed Designed in collaboration with Peter Gusmano for the Guitar for a Cure initiative $30 from each pedal donated to Project ALS Symmetry Switch for selectable clipping style Modified tone circuit for enhanced high-end clarity Boutique overdrive with unique tonal versatility and charitable purpose Reviews myFXDB user reviews No reviews yet + Add your review Links Keeley Electronics Keeley Drive For a Cure Where to find one? sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics Filaments High Gain Distortion
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Filaments High Gain Distortion - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu Keeley Electronics Filaments High Gain Distortion Posted By Pedal of the Day on Friday, January 26, 2018 in Keeley Electronics, Overdrive / Distortion | 0 comments --> --> Although we’re not the fastest or most technical of players around here, we sure can appreciate a good heavy metal tune, and the pedal we’re going to look at today is capable of providing the tones needed for speed, thrash, glam, black, death and other metal genres with ease. Robert and the kids at Keeley Electronics have covered just about all the bases when it comes to effects, and the Filaments High Gain Distortion is just another wicked rad box in their portfolio. Emulating high-gain tube amps and boasting an abundance of opportunities to yield crushing, ear-exploding tones, this is one aggressive and potent stompbox . Presenting you with 3 layered stages of gain and 7 different ways to EQ you tone, the Filaments is not light on tonal enhancement. Level and Gain do their jobs, respectively, both with a fat spectrum to play with and delve into. The Presence knob and the Bright toggle switch work in conjunction to provide a boost to any pickup configuration you may have, making all your guitars stand out, regardless of electronic layout. The two other toggles, Boost and Crunch, provide two differing gain and compression tones, making it fun to mix and match to find what works best for your amp and setup. The EQ section is where you can really dial this bad boy in. Bass and Treble adjust your low and high end frequencies, as expected, but there’s more for you to work with here. The Body knob fine-tunes more lows, giving you a fat and beefy but not muddied sound, and using the Treble knob right after it, your amp will project crisp metal lead runs, big, bold, sustained chords and even some tasty feedback if you want to toss that in as well. You can even run it at 18V for more headroom and louder production if that sort of thing gets your creative juices a-flowing. With the typical Keeley tough build and legendary quality, the Filaments Distortion is not a pedal you have to worry about breaking down, and is a road-worthy piece of your musical pie. Certainly not for everyone (no clean boost found here, people), the players in the genres it was designed for will really, really dig it, and should become a staple for heavy metal rigs for years to come. sources.description: Keeley Electronics Fuzz Bender: a versatile Tone Bender style fuzz spanning smooth and creamy to aggressive gated tones, with a massive EQ range.
sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics Fuzz Bender Demo Review | Loopy Demos
sources.bodyExcerpt: --> Keeley Electronics Fuzz Bender Demo Review | Loopy Demos Show or hide the side bar navigation Loopy Demos Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact Demos Posts Manufacturers About Contact All demos Keeley Electronics Fuzz Bender Mar 27, 2024 Read next What is the Best Velcro Fuzz Pedal? The Keeley Fuzz Bender is a three-transistor hybrid fuzz that uses both silicon and germanium stages to cover a lot of ground. At its tamest it sounds like an amp being pushed a little too hard. At its most extreme it gates, velcros and splutters in ways that feel almost alive. The real trick is that a three-band active EQ and a Bias control give you genuine surgical control over all of it, which is not something most Tone Bender-style circuits bother with. I like how the guitar melts into a full band mix with the Fuzz Bender. It doesn’t get drowned like it sometimes happens with Big Muffs in the wrong context. It provides this special texture to a track that makes it stand out and gives it character. Controls The panel puts the two main controls in a top row: Level on the left and Fuzz on the right, both large knobs. Below them sits a trio of smaller knobs: Bass, Bias, and Treble, running left to right. Level and Fuzz are the broad strokes; the middle row is where you fine-tune the character. Bass and Treble are gyrator-based active EQ with a swing of plus or minus 20dB each. That is a massive range. You can scoop the low end entirely or push it until the fuzz gets loose and wooly; Treble moves from flabby and dark to piercing and bright within the same gain setting. Bias is the wildcard: it adjusts the voltage reaching the transistors, which changes the feel of the attack. Pull it low and the fuzz blooms smoothly. Push it hard and the pedal starts to starve, gating notes and producing that velcro-ripping texture that people either love or can’t stand. In the demo above I’ve set up sweeps for the Bass, Bias, Treble, and Fuzz knobs so you can hear what each one does across its full range. How It Sounds The four named presets map the personality spread. Gnarly Bite runs the Bias high enough to put some edge on the attack without fully gating, which gives the fuzz a sharp front end that cuts through a mix. Spitty Fuzz cranks Fuzz all the way up and pushes Bias further, producing that classic starved-transistor velcro where notes decay with a sputtery tail. Warm Present pulls Bias back to zero and pushes the Fuzz and Bass controls, and the result is a rounder, smoother voice that earns the name. Full Drive is the overdrive-pedal-in-disguise setting: Fuzz low, Bass and Level up, Bias at zero. It sits surprisingly close to a cranked tweed amp at that setting. The germanium and silicon combination keeps the fuzz from being either purely vintage-dark or purely modern-bright. It lands somewhere in the middle, which makes it versatile but also a little easier to dial in than a purely germanium circuit. Fuzz Bender vs ZVEX Fuzz Factory The ZVEX Fuzz Factory is the other obvious gated-fuzz landmark, so it’s worth the comparison. Both pedals reach velcro territory and both reward dialing in. But the Fuzz Factory is a silicon-only circuit with five very interactive controls that affect each other in non-linear ways, and it can shift dramatically between guitars and pickups. The Fuzz Bender is more predictable: the EQ controls work independently and the Bias sweeps a defined range rather than feeding back on everything else. If you want wild and unpredictable, the Fuzz Factory goes further. If you want gated fuzz tones you can actually reproduce night to night, the Fuzz Bender is the more practical tool. I’ve put it head to head on the same loop with a few of these, so you can switch between them mid-phrase: Keeley Fuzz Bender vs Old Blood Noise Endeavors Alpha Haunt and Keeley Fuzz Bender vs ZVEX Fuzz Factory . The Fuzz Head is designed to work like Fuzz Face pedals that many players use as a LEAD BOOST. A Fuzz Face can be muddy, lacking note definition, too bassy, and lacking sustain. sources.h1: Keeley Electronics Announces The Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive: A Deep Technical and Musical Analysis for Guitarists and Keyboardists
sources.description: Keeley Electronics has launched the Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive — a dual-stage, true-bypass analog overdrive pedal combining vintage germanium transistor warmth with modern tonal flexibility. This article examines its circuit architecture, component-level specifications, real-world performance across guitar and keyboard applications, comparisons to classic units like the Colorsound Overdriver and Dallas Rangemaster, and measured frequency response data.
sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics Announces The Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive: A ...
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Announces The Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive: A Deep Technical and Musical Analysis for Guitarists and Keyboardists | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / piano piano Keeley Electronics Announces The Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive: A Deep Technical and Musical Analysis for Guitarists and Keyboardists By Liam Carter July 10, 2026 Introduction: A New Benchmark in Germanium-Driven Overdrive Keeley Electronics has officially unveiled the Germanium Super Phat Mod Overdrive — a meticulously engineered, dual-transistor overdrive pedal that redefines what’s possible with discrete germanium circuitry in the modern stompbox era. Unlike typical germanium-based pedals limited by temperature sensitivity and narrow headroom, this unit features matched OC44 and AC125 transistors (selected from batches tested at 25°C ±0.5°C), active bias stabilization, and a proprietary "Phat Mod" tone-shaping network that extends low-end response down to 48 Hz while preserving high-frequency clarity up to 12.3 kHz. However, rather than replicating these designs, Keeley’s engineering team reverse-engineered and optimized each stage for stability and dynamic range. Critical improvements include replacing the original Rangemaster’s passive emitter follower with an active, buffered output stage; adding thermally compensated bias resistors with ±1% metal film tolerance; and implementing a dual-rail virtual ground system that eliminates DC offset drift above 35°C ambient — a known failure point in vintage germanium units. Transistor Selection & Matching Protocol Keeley sources OC44 and AC125 transistors exclusively from NOS stock held in climate-controlled storage (18–22°C, 40–45% RH). Each batch undergoes rigorous binning: h FE is measured at 1 mA collector current with V CE = 1 V, and only units within 72–84 h FE are selected for the input stage (OC44) and 96–112 h FE for the output stage (AC125). Transistor pairs are matched to within ±3% h FE deviation and subjected to 72-hour thermal cycling (−10°C to +55°C) to verify long-term gain consistency. This protocol reduces unit-to-unit variance to under 0.8 dB across the full gain sweep — a dramatic improvement over vintage units, which routinely exhibit >4 dB variation. Notably, no electrolytic capacitors reside in the audio path; instead, 1% C0G ceramic and polypropylene film caps (WIMA MKP10) handle coupling and filtering. Power regulation uses a TPS7A47 ultra-low-noise LDO delivering ±0.02% ripple at 9V. sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Releases The Katana Blues Drive: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuitry, Tone, and Real-World Performance | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Keeley Electronics Releases The Katana Blues Drive: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuitry, Tone, and Real-World Performance By Nina Harper July 12, 2026 Introduction: A New Benchmark for Blues-Oriented Overdrive Keeley Electronics’ Katana Blues Drive is not just another overdrive pedal—it’s a meticulously engineered response to decades of player feedback about dynamic range compression, midrange smearing, and lack of touch-sensitive articulation in high-gain blues applications. Released in Q2 2024, the Katana Blues Drive features a discrete JFET front-end, dual independent gain paths (Clean Boost and Blues Drive), and a proprietary tonal architecture that preserves string definition at all output levels. Measuring 4.75" × 2.5" × 1.75" and weighing 198 grams, it fits seamlessly on crowded boards alongside pedals like the Ibanez Tube Screamer TS9, Wampler Euphoria, and Fulltone OCD v2. Unlike many boutique drives priced above $300, Keeley positions the Katana at $249—strategically bridging premium build quality and accessible functionality. Its true-bypass footswitch uses heavy-duty Cherry MX-style tactile switches rated for 10 million cycles, and internal circuitry runs on a regulated 9V DC supply with ultra-low-noise LDO regulators ( Design Philosophy and Historical Context Rob Keeley and his engineering team spent over 18 months reverse-engineering classic blues tone signatures—from Albert King’s 1967 Gibson ES-335 through a modified Fender Super Reverb to Stevie Ray Vaughan’s ’59 Stratocaster into a non-master-volume Marshall Plexi. Rather than emulate one specific amp, the Katana targets the interaction between guitar, pedal, and power amp: how dynamics compress, how harmonics bloom under pick attack, and how clean headroom collapses gracefully into saturation. Keeley explicitly cited three reference points: the early-’70s Colorsound Power Boost (notably its low-noise JFET input stage), the 1980s Ibanez AD80 (for its open midrange clarity), and the 2012 Analog Man Sunface (for its asymmetric clipping symmetry). Why ‘Katana’? Symbolism and Signal Path Intent The name isn’t merely aesthetic. In Japanese swordsmithing, a katana’s edge hardness (martensite) contrasts with its flexible spine (pearlite)—a duality Keeley mirrored in the pedal’s dual-path architecture. The Clean Boost path operates at +18dB maximum gain with near-zero coloration (±0.15dB deviation from 20Hz–20kHz), while the Blues Drive path delivers up to +28dB of musical asymmetrical clipping. Both paths share identical buffered inputs but diverge at the first transistor stage—eliminating crosstalk and preserving channel integrity. Physical Build and Component Selection Encased in CNC-machined 6061-T6 aluminum with powder-coated matte black finish, the Katana features gold-plated Neutrik NP2X jacks and a custom-designed 3PDT footswitch assembly. Internally, every resistor is metal-film (±0.1% tolerance), capacitors include Nichicon Muse FK series (audio-grade electrolytics) and WIMA FKP2 polypropylene film caps for critical coupling stages. The PCB uses 2-oz copper traces with dedicated ground planes beneath analog sections—reducing crosstalk by 22dB compared to Keeley’s prior layouts. Power regulation includes a Texas Instruments TPS7A47 LDO delivering stable 9.02V ±0.03V to all active components, verified across load ranges from 5mA to 120mA. Circuit Architecture Breakdown At its core, the Katana employs two cascaded JFET gain stages per channel—each using Toshiba 2SK30YT (J201 equivalent) transistors selected for V GS(off) consistency within ±0.15V. These are biased at 1.82V DC at the source, yielding optimal linearity for dynamic response. sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Katana Blues Drive Review: What Guitarists Need to Know | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / guitars guitars Keeley Katana Blues Drive Review: What Guitarists Need to Know By nina-harper June 30, 2026 Keeley Electronics Releases The Katana Blues Drive: What Guitarists Need to Know The Keeley Katana Blues Drive is a transparent, low-to-mid gain overdrive designed for dynamic responsiveness and amp-like feel—not stacking or high-gain saturation. For guitarists seeking authentic blues, classic rock, or clean-boosted tube amp tones—especially with Fender-style or lower-output humbucker rigs—the pedal delivers articulate breakup, touch-sensitive dynamics, and minimal coloration when bypassed. It excels when placed before a responsive tube amplifier (like a Fender Deluxe Reverb or Vox AC30), not as a standalone distortion source. Its relevance lies in solving a specific tonal need: preserving pick attack, string clarity, and harmonic richness while adding just enough grit to push an amp into singing territory— 🎸 🎯 🔊 . About Keeley Electronics Releases The Katana Blues Drive: Overview and Relevance to Guitar Players Released in late 2023, the Katana Blues Drive joins Keeley’s long-standing line of analog overdrives rooted in circuit-level fidelity rather than digital modeling or multi-function versatility. Unlike many modern drives that prioritize stacking capability or EQ flexibility, the Katana focuses on one task: delivering natural, amp-coupled overdrive at modest gain levels (0–6 on its Gain knob). Its core topology draws from vintage discrete transistor designs, notably inspired by the sound and response of early 1960s germanium boosters—but updated with modern silicon transistors for consistency and reliability 1 . It features three controls: Gain, Tone, and Volume, plus true bypass switching and a compact 9V DC power requirement (no battery option). For guitarists, its relevance emerges in context: it does not replace a cranked tube amp, nor does it emulate one digitally. Instead, it behaves like a well-placed preamp stage—enhancing headroom compression, tightening low-end response, and sharpening transient articulation without masking fundamental frequencies. This makes it especially useful for players using lower-wattage amps (15W and under), studio tracking where amp volume must stay low, or live situations requiring consistent drive texture across setlists. Why This Matters: Benefits for Tone, Playability, and Knowledge The Katana Blues Drive matters because it reinforces foundational concepts often obscured by feature-rich pedals: signal integrity, gain staging discipline, and interaction between guitar, pedal, and amplifier. Its transparency teaches players how much their instrument’s output level, pickup type, and cable capacitance affect drive onset—and how subtle adjustments (e.g., rolling back guitar volume) yield dramatic tonal shifts. In practice, this means: Tone: Maintains note separation during chords, preserves harmonic overtones on single-note lines, and avoids midrange congestion common in op-amp-based drives. Playability: Responds dynamically to picking force—light strumming stays clean; aggressive downstrokes bloom into saturated warmth—without lag or compression artifacts. Knowledge: Demonstrates how gain placement affects overall system behavior. When used before the amp’s input (not in the loop), it interacts directly with the preamp stage, affecting both EQ balance and power-amp sag characteristics. This isn’t a ‘set-and-forget’ effect—it invites active engagement. That pedagogical dimension separates it from utility pedals. Heavy Gain, Soft Focus, Reverse, Cascading Octave Feedback, Tremolo Bar Strummed Reverb. A stoned, morning floaty, messed up, thrill machine is what it is. Washes of reverb in new ways youve not heard in a stomp box before and a fuzz thats like a cigarette burn on your forearm. It rages. Jesus, Mary, and Reverbs Cant live without these three and the new reverbs are born of a Shoegaze dream. Hall Super long ambient wash with the ability to add octave regeneration in the feedback loop. More than shimmer its more like ascension shimmer. Reverse Set different delay times with the Decay control which gives you rhythmic reverse. This is based on the Yamaha SPX90 and the Alesis Midiverb II. This is not a true reversed reverb as it reads through a delay line at various points in the delay while increasing in volume. The Decay control is more of a switch in that it is chooshing between 8 different set decay times: 150ms, 200ms, 250ms, 300ms, 350ms, 400ms, 450ms, and 500ms allowing you to set all kinds of delay times in which the notes come back at you. This is where it gets really cool. The vibrato in this mode is envelope controlled. The range runs from 0 to 50ms of time shift.Tone control is loosely based on the Jazzmaster rhythm tone control with a low pass filter centered at 156.6Hz Strum hard at it pitch bends like you are playing the trem bar on a Jazzmaster or Jaguar! Combine the two for an unreal dual-guitar player effect! Soft Focus Because all of the reverbs can go All-Wet by means of the Blend Control, this is a great approximation of the Yamaha FX500 patch. Soft Focus Reverb features a dense reverb with two delays in parallel (one set for 250ms, the other set for 380ms.)” Shipping Info Standard Shipping Cost: $25 Free Shipping We offer free shipping on orders over $30. Qty: Email a Friend Print Page FREE Shipping in the U.S.! • Evolution of the legendary transparent overdrive • NOS germanium transistors diodes for rich saturation • Bass+ switch adds low-end punch (+3dB) • Ge-Trans switch enhances tube-like compression • Selectable True Bypass or Buffered Silent Switching • 18V-ready for massive headroom • Handcrafted in the USA The Keeley Manis Overdrive uniquely combines both germanium NOS transistors and diodes for more compression and saturation plus a 3db bass-boost makes it unlike any other mythical Klone! Keeley pens the next chapter in the legend of the mythical Klone with several storied upgrades and features. First up is the germanium diode switch. The “essential” germanium diodes are at the heart of the myth. By substituting essential germanium diodes with germanium transistors (circa Cold War era) we increase the compression and saturation of the tone. The Manis can give you a softer attack that sounds more like a tube amp. Less ice-pick, more tube amp. This feels incredible under your fingertips too. Wouldn’t you like to hear a little more of the natural low end from your guitar? The bass boost switch lowers the cutoff by exactly one octave and increases the output by +3dB. It’s the perfect low end recovery and push for single coil guitars. True Bypass or Buffered Silent Switching on the fly. The Manis is built like a tank and is the first klone you can power with 18 volts. The Manis is a Hard Clipping ‘clean boost’ that has been updated and modernized with our power supply improvements as well as other mind bending fixes to the inherent tonal problems of the original circuit. The Manis is Hard Clipping “clean boost” using Russian transistors as germanium diodes Ge-Trans Switch – Diodes or Transistors – Huge difference in feel with increased saturation and tube like compression The Bass+ Switch – Lowers the frequency response by one octave and then pushes 3dB harder True-Bypass or Buffered Bypass/silent Switching – Whichever works and sounds best in your rig. Switchable Germanium Diodes Germanium is a rare earth metal. The Manis has both germanium diodes and transistors, significantly increasing the chances of making rarified music Switchable Low Frequency Cutoff | The Manis Overdrive lets you fatten your bottom end in a sensible way. Buffered Bypass or True Bypass The Keeley Manis Overdrive allows you to quickly switch between either mode. Having a great buffer will make your rig sound strong and clear even when the pedal is off. Keeley Electronics Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe (3 customer reviews) $394.90 $149.00 Keeley Electronics Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe, new."The Keeley Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibehas a vintage fuzz, rotary speaker, vibe, harmonic and auto wah, an octave up or octave down, as wellan expression control to allow you to create a rich array of new and Add to cart SKU: AKHQ36745 Category: Effect Description Additional information Reviews Introduction Keeley Electronics Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe, new. “The Keeley Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibehas a vintage fuzz, rotary speaker, vibe, harmonic and auto wah, an octave up or octave down, as wellan expression control to allow you to create a rich array of new and newer sounds. There are two channels on the Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe, and these can be configured to give you five different sounds. The right stomp switch activates the fuzz channel. The fuzz channel has been designed to give you a rich, full, classic two-transistor fuzz sound that is accurate yet has a touch of smoothness added. It is very responsive and dynamic. It plays well in any position on a Strat or Les Paul style guitar. At the heart of the fuzz are vintage Fairchild Semiconductor transistors. These moderate gain transistors offer the perfect fuzz tone and do not have the temperamental temperature related problems that germanium devices exhibit, while still giving you incredible tone. The modulation channel is where the fun really starts. The Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe offers an Octave effect with both the Vibe and Wah sounds. With those two sounds you can either have Octave Up, Octave Down, or No Octave. In the Center Position of the Octave Control you have NOoctave up or down. If you turn the Octave Control up (or clockwise), you have an increasing octave up sound. As you turn the Octave Control down, you have an increasing amount of octave down sound added. Again, if you do not want an octave effect added, simply set the Octave Control to the center position. The Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe features a very rich and deep vibe sound. The Kool Vibe setting is perfect for getting complex phaser-like sounds. It combines phasing and tremolo at key frequencies to give you incredible depth and rhythm. Not only does it match the frequency response of a vibe, it simulates the unique pulsing of a photo-cell based effect. You can add the Octave to the Kool Vibefor an amazing doublingeffect or for an incredibly deep synth bass type sound. "The Keeley Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibehas a vintage fuzz, rotary speaker, vibe, harmonic and auto wah, an octave up or octave down, as wellan expression control to allow you to create a rich array of new and newer sounds. There are two channels on the Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe, and these can be configured to give you five different sounds. The right stomp switch activates the fuzz channel. The fuzz channel has been designed to give you a rich, full, classic two-transistor fuzz sound that is accurate yet has a touch of smoothness added. It is very responsive and dynamic. It plays well in any position on a Strat or Les Paul style guitar. At the heart of the fuzz are vintage Fairchild Semiconductor transistors. These moderate gain transistors offer the perfect fuzz tone and do not have the temperamental temperature related problems that germanium devices exhibit, while still giving you incredible tone. The modulation channel is where the fun really starts. The Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe offers an Octave effect with both the Vibe and Wah sounds. With those two sounds you can either have Octave Up, Octave Down, or No Octave. In the Center Position of the Octave Control you have NOoctave up or down. If you turn the Octave Control up (or clockwise), you have an increasing octave up sound. As you turn the Octave Control down, you have an increasing amount of octave down sound added. Again, if you do not want an octave effect added, simply set the Octave Control to the center position. The Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe features a very rich and deep vibe sound. The Kool Vibe setting is perfect for getting complex phaser-like sounds. It combines phasing and tremolo at key frequencies to give you incredible depth and rhythm. Not only does it match the frequency response of a vibe, it simulates the unique pulsing of a photo-cell based effect. You can add the Octave to the Kool Vibefor an amazing doublingeffect or for an incredibly deep synth bass type sound. The Les Rotary sound in the Monterey Fuzz Vibe is both very accurate and surprisingly new sounding. Like the original cabinet, this simulation joinsboth the lowerdrum and the upper horn into a rich, dimensionaleffect that generates anunmistakable chorus and tremolo soundscape. Not only is the cabinet itself simulated with very short reverberated reflections that offer a doubling effect, the Doppler Effect provides a soothing chorused sound that is clean and ethereal. The Octave Control in the Rotary cabinet simulation controls the volume of the horn or tweeter sounds. It does not produce an octave effect here. This allows you to get a very chorus-like effect with amplehigh-end detail when simulating a Les Rotary style cabinet. Set the Rate OFFfor no rotation, turn the Fuzz on, and the Depth and Octave controls give you a wonderful speaker cabinet simulation. Its fuzz with tonal control like youve never had before! Perfect for matching any size of power amp with the pedals fuzz to give you anythingfrom dark overdrive to hard, edgy, squared fuzz! The Harmonic Wah section combines several more new sounds from Keeley in the Monterey Rotary Fuzz Vibe. It is a fixed or cocked wah sound, an auto wah, a harmonic/tremolo wah, and even a regular foot-controlled wah when you add an expression pedal. Live on WhatNot at 6pm Central → LEARN MORE Home Pedals and Effects Pedals and Effects Fuzz Keeley Electronics Moon Fuzz Keeley Moon Op Amp Fuzz Overview The Keeley Moon Op Amp Fuzz is a supermassive fuzz pedal built to deliver crushing low end, soaring sustain, and harmonically rich chaos. Designed for players who want their tone to feel as heavy as gravity itself, the Moon Op Amp Fuzz pushes both guitar and bass frequencies into deep, punishing territory while still retaining clarity and musicality. This is not a polite fuzz. It’s a galaxy-spinning, feedback-inducing op amp monster that thrives in heavy riffs, massive walls of sound, and infinite, dreamy sustain. Massive Op Amp Fuzz Tone At the heart of the Moon Op Amp Fuzz is a quad op amp circuit that delivers four stages of gain and fuzz . Drawing inspiration from Keeley’s Dark Side pedal, this design flips the concept entirely—moving away from vintage lead fuzz and straight into thick, modern, low-frequency devastation. The result is an op amp fuzz that extends your instrument’s frequencies as low as possible while keeping upper harmonics rich and alive. Notes bloom, rise, and peak into expressive feedback with ease. Expanded Filter Control EQ Modes The Moon Op Amp Fuzz offers an expanded filter control that provides a wide range of usable tones, from tight and focused to wide-open and massive. A dedicated filter switch lets you choose between three distinct EQ phases: Scooped Mids (Classic): Perfect for massive, aggressive fuzz tones with a familiar heavy character Flat EQ: Balanced and versatile for cutting through mixes Full Range: Maximum depth, clarity, and low-end extension These options make the Moon Op Amp Fuzz adaptable across genres, from doom and sludge to shoegaze and experimental rock. sources.title: Keeley Electronics Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost | AllThePedals
sources.description: The Keeley Electronics Noble Screamer is a 4-in-1 overdrive and boost pedal designed to deliver a wide range of tones. This versatile pedal offers two familiar drive circuits alongside two new amp-like distortion options, all in a single, user-friendly unit. It features switchable diode clipping, tone controls, and buffered or true bypass switching for enhanced flexibility. The Noble Screamer allows guitarists to create unique hybrid sounds, blending classic overdrive effects with innovative new tones. It's inspired by the classic [Ibanez Tube Screamer](/pedals/ibanez-tube-screamer-mini-overdrive) but takes the concept further, offering a range of tones and features to inspire players.

sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Overdrive / Keeley Electronics Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost The Keeley Electronics Noble Screamer is a 4-in-1 overdrive and boost pedal designed to deliver a wide range of tones. This versatile pedal offers two familiar drive circuits alongside two new amp-like distortion options, all in a single, user-friendly unit. It features switchable diode clipping, tone controls, and buffered or true bypass switching for enhanced flexibility. The Noble Screamer allows guitarists to create unique hybrid sounds, blending classic overdrive effects with innovative new tones. It's inspired by the classic Ibanez Tube Screamer but takes the concept further, offering a range of tones and features to inspire players. What Keeley Electronics say about the Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost 4-in-1 Overdrive and Boost Two all-new amp-like hybrid tones All analog signal path Switch from Buffered to True Bypass on the fly All new proprietary case shape – manufactured by RKFX in the USA Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost Imagine being able to combine your favorite parts of different overdrive boost pedals in order to create hybrid sounds no one has ever played through before. That is exactly what we’ve engineered with the Noble Screamer. It’s a 4-in-1 pedal that gives you two very familiar drive circuits and two brand new amp-like distortion tones that no one has used before. It’s almost like pedal-modeling, except these are 100% analog circuits, and you decide which tone-control or clipping-section you want to play through. You can play through battle-tested, classic overdrive effects or innovate new music with hybrid tones, let your ears be the judge. Even with all of these features the pedal remains a simple and easy to use three knob overdrive. The innovation in the Noble Screamer doesn’t end there; our new design features true-bypass or buffered, truly silent switching, on the fly. The Keeley Noble Screamer Overdrive and Boost is entirely manufactured at Keeley Electronics and is the first in our new aluminum enclosure. Four Overdrive and Boost sounds – including two new, amp-like hybrid tones Silent Buffered Bypass or True Bypass – hold down foot switch to change quickly Professionally Engineered Tone – sounds developed in the field and in our tone lab Tone Control Broad Spectrum Tone Control or Narrow Focus Filter Control: The Noble Screamer gives you two tone control circuits to choose from. When the Tone Switch is up and in the OD Position you will hear a ‘Spectrum’ type of tone control that has the ability to go from a flat EQ to an EQ that has a boost in the treble and bass response. If the Tone Switch is in the TS Position you have a Low Pass Filter that rolls off the high frequencies only. Diode Clipping Hard or Soft Clipping: The Noble Screamer gives you both styles of diode clipping. Diodes are used to create hard clipping distortions or smooth overdrive sounds. If the Clipping Switch is in the OD Position it features Hard Diode Clipping which is an edgier, more aggressive tone. When the Clipping Switch is in the TS Position that uses Soft Diode Clipping, like a tube amplifier softly overdriven. Noble Screamer Has Both Buffered and True Bypass The Keeley Noble Screamer features our Vitamin K Infused Buffer for noise free switching. We have developed an amazing sounding buffer which not only makes your rig sound better, it gives you silent switching with no tone loss. No more pops and clicks to distract from your music. FOR SALE! Keeley Electronics Oxblood Germanium Overdrive – LIMITED EDITION with Mullard OC75 germanium transistors I think Keeley only made about 60 of these. This one is number 40. Keely has only making these as parts are available. Mullard OC75 germanium transistors are quite rare now-a-days so these pedals are quite limited in production. This version of the Oxblood make a great pedal even better. I liked my regular production model Oxblood so much that I jumped at the chance to grab the Germanium version when I saw one for sale. Keeley Oxblood Overdrive is a super versatile boost, overdrive and distortion in ONE pedal. This pedal has the utmost versatility with the minimum of tweaks needed. From clean boost to overdrive to distortion in one pedal. The PHAT and Clipping switches make some nice sound! From Robert Keeley: We’ve taken out the compression and added a germanium transistor to the output. Bolder and Smoother! With less compression now, the Oxblood Germanium Overdrive sounds more like a true and flattens out the mid-range. Next we couldn’t help adding a touch of our favorite germanium transistor, the OC75 by Mullard! This takes out any harness from that release of compression. I call it perfection. Oh, and these are 100% hand built. The craftsmen and designers at Keeley wanted this to be our finest and loudest moment, so we made it in the “Thunder” color scheme. AND, this is the first run of cases we powder coated in house! A first for Keeley that we are very proud of! The Oxblood Germanium Overdrive is our response to everyone cloning the “Mythical Beast” pedal. We decided to build an original design. We wanted to build a new circuit that let players blend from perfectly clean to amp-crushing roar. We wanted that impossibly huge and focused midrange that makes any guitar… Strat, Paul, Tele, sound incredible. We knew we could do it our way and offer you more tone. So we designed this pedal over the course of a few days to outdo the old pedal. I am confident we not only drew blood, we crafted a #killer Clean, Distortion, Fuzz – It’s All There With the Oxblood Germanium Overdrive you roll off the Drive Control down and get a perfectly clean sound, you can dial in any amount of distortion and volume to stomp an amp into pure tonal nirvana. The Keeley Oxblood Germanium Overdrive offers you two ways to clip and saturate your signal with overtones by selecting carefully chosen diodes, these are different than the standard Oxblood. These were chosen to give you bigger more open amp tones, without a lot of compression. The key to the ultimate overdrive in our opinion is the ability to control five different parameters. Bass response. Phat Switch, cuts bass response to give you that classic Screamer or K-like midrange shelving. The bass response when cut is saturated with a hint of 2nd order harmonics. Punchy and full yet not overbearing. It cuts like a buffalo, what can I say? Clipping. Sometimes there just ain’t enough gain in the world. Well not with this beast. The Clipping Switch gives you the ability to sing with near infinite sustain or just stand on your amp like a chief. From Texas Rock to Bold Pretty Boy Strat Sounds that make ya wanna die. Heck we give you the range to do whatever the heck you want to do. Volume. You have to be able to put the pedal to the metal whenever you darn well chose. Product Description Keeley Red Dirt Mini Pedal In a time long ago, 2001 to be exact, Keeleyâ€™s mods for the TS9 Tube Screamer became pretty legendary. Â They set the standard for a complete set of changes, a dozen in fact, that took any screamer to the next level. Â Â Those mods included an increased bass response, a fine-tuned tone control, greater cleans when turned down, and much higher gain when needed. Â The Keeley Mod Plus was born. In fact the mod was crafted so well that it didnâ€™t change one bit in nearly 14 years. Â The circuit and mods have been on some incredible stages, Steve Vai, Joe Satriani, Brad Paisley, John Petrucci, heck who hasnâ€™t toured with a Keeley TS Mod in the 2000â€™s The Red Dirt came out in 2012 and is currently on tour with John Petrucci and Devin Townsend to name just a few. Â It is essentially all of the Keeley mods wrapped into one pedal. Â It also features one really important addition, the JFET input buffer. Â A mod that couldnâ€™t be done to the old screamers is a JFET input buffer change. Â Now the Red Dirt and Red Dirt Mini are more open and dynamicâ€¦ and let your pickups breathe in a way that youâ€™ve not heard. Four Modes The four modes of operation are completely new for the Red Dirt Mini. Â The pedalâ€™s base-line tone is configured by taking the bottom plate off and adjusting the DIP switches. Â These switches allow you to change the clipping diodes which give you either a more compressed sound, or give you a more open tube-amp like sound and variations in between. Â The different overdrive styles are: Distortion, Overdrive, Crunch, and Amp. Â Going from the high gain Distortion Mode where you have 2 to 3 times screamer gain, they give you progressively cleaner, more open and bolder sounds. Â The Red Dirt Mini is huge on tone and flexibility. Red Dirt Mini Size and Power Huge tone and small size in the Red Dirt Mini. Â Itâ€™s the working manâ€™s overdrive in a small package, just 1.5â€² x 3.6â€² Â Needs only a 9 volt negative-tip power supply and 7.5mA of current. sources.h1: Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog Pedalboard Revolution
sources.description: Keeley Electronics has unveiled the Tone Workstation — a 19-inch rack-mountable, modular analog effects platform featuring four independent stereo channels, 12V DC power distribution, integrated expression pedal inputs, and support for up to eight simultaneously active analog pedals with true-bypass routing. Designed for studio engineers, touring guitarists, and pedalboard architects, it replaces traditional looper-based switching with voltage-controlled analog signal path management.
sources.snippet: Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog ...
sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog Pedalboard Revolution | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Keeley Electronics Announces The Tone Workstation: A Modular Analog Pedalboard Revolution By Liam Carter July 15, 2026 What Is the Tone Workstation? Keeley Electronics’ Tone Workstation is not another multi-effects unit or digital processor. It is a purpose-built, analog-centric hardware platform that redefines how guitarists and bass players manage complex pedal configurations. Unveiled at the 2024 NAMM Show in Anaheim, the Tone Workstation is a 3U (5.25-inch tall) 19-inch rack-mounted device weighing 12.8 pounds and measuring 17.25 × 13.5 × 6.5 inches (W × D × H). Unlike conventional loop switchers such as the Boss ES-8 or TC Electronic Nexus, the Tone Workstation integrates analog signal path control, real-time voltage-based modulation routing, and built-in power regulation into a single chassis — all without digitizing the audio path. The core architecture centers on four fully independent stereo channels, each with its own dedicated input/output pair, buffered bypass circuitry, and assignable expression CV (control voltage) output. Each channel supports up to two analog effect modules — meaning the system can host up to eight discrete analog pedals simultaneously while maintaining true analog signal integrity from input to output. Keeley confirmed zero digital conversion occurs in the audio path; all switching, gain staging, and level balancing happen entirely in the analog domain using discrete JFETs and low-noise op-amps (Texas Instruments OPA2134 and OPA1612). Crucially, the Tone Workstation does not require external power supplies for connected pedals. Its internal 12V DC power distribution system delivers regulated, filtered, and isolated outputs: eight 9V DC (center-negative) ports rated at 300mA each, two 12V DC (center-negative) ports at 500mA, and one 18V DC port at 400mA — sufficient to power high-current devices like the Strymon Big Sky, Empress Effects Reverb, or Walrus Audio Mako Series without noise bleed or voltage sag. Hardware Design & Physical Interface Keeley’s industrial design team collaborated with aerospace-grade enclosure manufacturer Bud Industries to fabricate the chassis from 1.2mm cold-rolled steel with powder-coated matte black finish. Front-panel controls consist of 16 tactile, gold-plated Alps RK09K rotary encoders (four per channel), eight LED-lit footswitches (two per channel), and dual high-resolution OLED displays (128 × 64 pixels each) showing real-time signal metrics including input/output level (−40dBV to +10dBV), channel mute status, and expression pedal position (0–100%). Each channel features three physical I/O connectors: a ¼” TRS input, a ¼” TRS output, and a 3.5mm stereo expression input. Rear-panel connectivity expands functionality significantly: two balanced XLR inputs/outputs (switchable between line-level and instrument-level via rear DIP switches), MIDI IN/OUT/THRU ports compliant with MIDI 1.0 specification, USB-C host port for firmware updates (not audio streaming), and an Ethernet port supporting OSC (Open Sound Control) over LAN for integration with Ableton Live, MainStage, or custom control software. Power Architecture Deep Dive The internal power supply uses a toroidal transformer coupled with six independent linear regulators — one per 9V rail plus dedicated regulators for 12V and 18V outputs. Ripple suppression measures below 150µV RMS across all rails, verified by Keysight DSOX2004A oscilloscope testing at full load. This exceeds industry benchmarks set by Voodoo Lab Ground Control Pro (220µV) and Eventide UltraSwitch (180µV). All power outputs are individually fused with slow-blow 350mA ceramic fuses, preventing cascade failures. sources.bodyExcerpt: Keeley | Tone Workstation Multi-Effects - Sugaree Licks Skip to content Menu Cart Sugaree Licks Cart Search All Amps All Pedals All Guitars Songs Albums Artists Submit Submit A Song Add An Album To Sugaree Licks Add An Artist To Sugaree Licks Equipment For Sale Clearance Pedals Amps All Amps Top Amps Submit An Amp Pedals All Pedals Top Pedals Submit A Pedal Guitars All Guitars Top Guitars Submit A Guitar Manufacturers All Manufacturers Submit A Manufacturer GET Guitar Equipment Terminology Chords Guitar Chords A Guitar Chords B Guitar Chords C Guitar Chords D Guitar Chords E Guitar Chords F Guitar Chords G SHOP Widgets User Account Username or Email Password Remember Me or REGISTER Close Menu Close Cart Keeley | Tone Workstation Multi-Effects by Sweetwater Website Link Keeley Website Link Model Number or Name: Tone Workstation Boost Compression Multi-Effect Overdrive Circuit Type: Analog Electrical Components: JFET Transistor Original Price: $299 Excellent Used Price: $230 Year Released: 2015 Alternate Version(s) No Alternate Versions Listed Ten years ago we invented and built a small batch of the Tone Workstation, which then moved into the hands of famous players and collectors. John Mayer recently took two of the originals out on the Dead Company tour. For 2016 it’s more than a re-release; it’s a completely new, re-engineered workstation. The Keeley team of engineers and designers have upgraded the tone, enhanced the features, and reduced the size to now fit on anyone’s board. Introducing the Tone Workstation The front end of your signal chain–this is where your tone develops. The first stage of amplification is critical for a sound that has clarity and delivers expressive tone. Compression, Drive, Overdrive, Boost: you get it all here. The Tone Workstation is designed to be the first stage in your pedal board. It may even be the only pedal you bring to a gig. And we designed it that way. Starting with the classic Keeley Compressor, you can build a nice, thick tone full of sustain. Adjust the Sustain control for increased compression or squeeze. As you add sustain, your notes will ring out longer. The Blend control allows for a Manhattan-style compression, keeping the sound lively and crisp as you blend in your natural guitar tone. The Blend control is perfect for adding a little bit of bite back in with high output pickups or humbuckers. In addition, the Treble Boost switch can be engaged to further increase the treble and sparkle into the signal when using lots of compression. When the Blend is set completely CCW, you get only compressed signal out. Then, as you turn up the Blend, you blend in more and more of your original signal, all the way to a 50/50 ratio. The attack and release times are pre-set in this compressor and are set for use with humbuckers or single coils. Next up is the 1962/Katana Boost section, because the Keeley Workstation gives you plenty of options for your core tone. With the 62/Katana channel, you can select a sound with just the right amount of break up. Or use it in Boost mode, for that clean, pushed amp-style overdrive. First, the 1962 is our British amp-style overdrive, which is full and even sounding with a moderate amount of crunch. Based on the famous Blues Breaker, the 1962 stage has been amplified by our Katana Boost on either side, adding tube-like saturation with our JFET valve simulation. But, decide you just want the famous Katana Clean push? No worries. Just a flick of the switch and you have it: pure clean, tube tone. In the Katana Mode, only the volume works; the Tone and Drive are disabled. It’s a clean sound people say you just can’t turn off. Last in the chain is our renowned Red Dirt overdrive. You get 15 years of modding tube screamers distilled into one toneful circuit. Also featuring our JFET front end, the Red Dirt has the perfect amount of crucial midrange coupled with the option to go all the way from clean and clear to super-saturated gain, times two! The tone of Dark Blood is tube-like and mid-heavy with added high gain. It’s unique power is its distinctly amp-like sound. Richly articulate and deep, Dark Blood can provide the main tone into your clean amp and is ideal as a fly rig and a backup to an amp or modeling rig. With its high gain and aggressive, uncompromising dynamics, this is the ultimate pedal for gain-freaks, designed both for palm muting riffs and searing high gain solos. KHDK Electronics Dark Blood Distortion Effect Pedal quantity Add to cart Free shipping on orders over $40 100% Secure & Encrypted Payments Categories: Effects Description Reviews (0) Looking for a heavy-duty drive box that will give you amp-like tones with the added benefit of a built-in noise gate? The KHDK Electronics Dark Blood is an excellent choice then. This high gain pedal is an original circuit from KHDK that combines solid state and mosfet technology to create a distortion that will give you the gain you need through any amp you run it through.Doom controls the pre-distortion equalization which determines the amount of low-end grunt present in your tone. This control moves from a tight bass to a long sustain, giving you a liquid, solo-ready tone.Gate controls the background noise of your tone. This allows the stronger gain signal to pass, while weaker humming or hissing is blocked. Turn the gate clockwise for noise reduction, but avoid pushing the gate with lower gain settings; this could negatively impact the decay of your tone.Gain controls the gain of the circuit. A lower setting creates a pick-sensitive tone with excellent dynamics, while a higher setting brings a massively overdriven tone.Treble Control is a passive, natural sounding low-pass filter. It cuts high end and offers a wide frequency range. Turned clockwise, it becomes raw, aggressive and cuts through. Turned counterclockwise, it cuts highs for a warmer and more mellow tone. With different amps, the tone can be bright or dark; use this control to set the ideal amount of brightness/top end.Volume sets the output volume of the pedal. Warning: at higher settings, the Dark Blood has a massive output. This pedal gets LOUD!LO/HI is tied directly into the gain and offers two steps of gain. LO is intended for rhythm playing while HI adds saturation, sustain, and compression. HI setting is recommended for a more powerful rhythm or soloing. sources.description: A detailed, musician-first review of the KHDK Ghoul Screamer — covering tone accuracy, build durability, pedalboard fit, and real-world performance in studio and live settings.
sources.snippet: Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review: Honest Tone, Build Use Analysis
sources.bodyExcerpt: Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review: Honest Tone, Build Use Analysis | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review: Honest Tone, Build Use Analysis By zoe-langford June 18, 2026 Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review The KHDK Ghoul Screamer is a high-gain overdrive/distortion pedal designed for articulate, dynamic saturation—not just volume or noise. In our Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review , we found it delivers exceptional touch sensitivity and harmonic complexity at medium to high gain, but demands careful EQ pairing and isn’t ideal for low-headroom amps or players seeking simple, one-knob distortion. It excels in studio rhythm tracking and expressive lead work when paired with clean or slightly broken-up tube amps—making it a strong candidate for discerning rock, blues-rock, and modern indie guitarists who prioritize note definition over brute force. About Quick Hit Khdk Ghoul Screamer Review: Product Background KHDK Electronics is a boutique pedal manufacturer co-founded by guitarist Kirk Hammett (Metallica) and designer Dimitris Kourtis. Launched in 2014, the company focuses on high-fidelity analog circuits built around discrete transistors and hand-selected components. The Ghoul Screamer—introduced in late 2021—sits between KHDK’s earlier Love Pedal Eternity (a transparent boost/overdrive) and the heavier, more saturated Ghetto Blaster. Unlike many “Screamer”-style pedals inspired by the Ibanez Tube Screamer, the Ghoul Screamer diverges significantly in topology: it uses a dual-stage JFET-driven gain structure with active tone shaping, rather than the classic op-amp-based clipping circuit. Its stated goal is to deliver “dynamic, harmonically rich overdrive that cleans up with guitar volume without collapsing into thinness”—a claim rooted in its input impedance design and cascaded gain staging. First Impressions: Build Quality, Initial Setup, Design Unboxing reveals a compact, rugged enclosure: 4.5" × 2.75" × 1.75", matte black anodized aluminum housing with laser-etched labeling. The chassis feels dense and substantial—no flex or panel warping. All controls (Gain, Tone, Volume, Voice) are sealed, industrial-grade Alpha pots with tactile detents; the footswitch is a heavy-duty, true-bypass, soft-click switch with LED indicator (blue when engaged). No battery compartment—the Ghoul Screamer requires a regulated 9V DC power supply (center-negative, 100mA minimum); no internal battery option exists, which simplifies internal layout but eliminates portable use. The PCB is fully hand-soldered with through-hole components, including custom-wound inductors and film capacitors visible under the top plate. A small, recessed trimpot labeled "HF Trim" sits inside the battery compartment cover (though unused unless modified)—a nod to KHDK’s service-oriented design philosophy. Detailed Specifications Below is a complete specification breakdown, contextualized for practical use: 🎸 Input Impedance: 1.2 MΩ — unusually high, preserving treble response from passive pickups and reducing loading effects on buffered pedals upstream. 🔊 Output Impedance: 150 Ω — low enough to drive long cable runs and multiple downstream pedals without tone loss. ⚡ Power Requirement: 9V DC, center-negative, regulated supply only; draws ~52 mA — compatible with most modern isolated power supplies (e.g., Strymon Zuma, Voodoo Lab Pedal Power 2+). 🎛️ Controls: Gain (0–10), Tone (0–10), Volume (0–10), Voice (0–10). Voice adjusts midrange contour—0 emphasizes upper-mids (“cutting”), 10 leans into lower-mids (“thickening”). 🔌 Signal Path: True bypass via mechanical relay switching (no pop/click on engagement), with status LED. 📏 Dimensions & Weight: 114 × 70 × 44 mm; 385 g — heavier than average due to thick metal chassis and transformerless power regulation. 🔄 Circuit Type: Discrete, Class-A JFET preamp stage feeding a second JFET clipping stage; no op-amps in audio pa

This is about recreating the sounds that made me want to play guitar in the first place." Read the story of how we collabed with Zacky on this absolute monster of a pedal. Down-low: this limited edition is a high-gain preamp celebrating Zacky's tone, punk rock and metal The gain and fuzz are 100% independent of each other. This means that you can mix in as much or little into your signal, from 0 to 100. You can adjust the amount of distortion and gain using the knobs to adjust the amount of aggression. CONTROLS: Gain // Bass // Treble // Drive // Fuzz // Volume // Bypass Each pedal is built and guitar-tested in the KHDK workshop in the EU, featuring original zombie artwork by the great Mario Lopez. Zacky personally signed all Certificates of Authenticity that ship with each pedal, so you know you're getting the real deal! Explore the tone Controls Specs Controls Specs Full rundown of Night of the Living Shred Controls GAIN sets your pre-gain. There is a mellow crunch, just like chewing on a delicious femur. Zacky recommends that you balance the setting with your DRIVE and VOLUME (in the Overdrive section) as these act symbiotically. BASS and TREBLE give you an amp-like response. Powered by KHDK's original circuit, the No.1 is designed in the spirit of an overdriven tube amp. Turn the No.1 on and you'll feel like you've switched to a powerful distortion channel on a tube amp. "I plugged it in and was instantly knocked out. It's a very amp overdrive-like pedal." – Pete Thorn The No.1's unique feature is its double gain control One just wasn't enough! That's why we built No.1 with two gain controls. Gain one controls the first gain stage from a pure clean boost to a naturally compressing overdrive. Gain two shares one knob with the Bass control. It cleverly controls the gain and the low-end of the next gain stage, which adds rich harmonics, bottom end, and natural tube-like saturation to your tone. It's designed as an active high-pass filter for the second gain stage and allows you to set the amount of bottom-end with precision. The result is rich, harmonic overdrive. It's versatile and bold: with the Gain switch on Lo, the No.1 ranges from a barely-breaking-up overdrive to a classic crunch. Set the Gain on Hi and you can take it from an aggressive, dirty rhythm tone all the way up to a beautiful lead tone. Technology No.1 utilizes KHDK's original true bypass circuit using our special blend of solid state and mosfet technology. The second iteration of the legendary SHRED, his new and improved brother has arrived: say hello to SHRED 2! 100% clarity, 100% power, 0% compromise - Bernth’s SHRED solves the age-old problem of having to compromise tonal power for clarity. With Shred, you can finally have both. A collector's piece for your pedalboard SHRED comes with a haunting artwork based on the winning vote of Bernth’s community. Limited 250 pcs Edition Overdrive for your Guitar and Bass Designed with Slipknot's Alessandro Venturella, Totality gives you the VMan's signature powerful and aggressive sound, perfect for metal and rock playing and fast riffing. Totality is a mixing board for your amp and overdriven tone, with a dual-path input Alessandro brought his years of technical knowhow to the table and helped create the Totality as a dual-path OD pedal for guitar and bass, so you can switch it up depending on your mood. This OD gets gritty as fuck, so it is totally different than anything we have done before Your signal is split into two paths, with controls GAIN, TONE, BASS and TREBLE along the way...and, it has a mid switch tuned to Alessandro's preferences, so you can get that sweet, sweet heavy as fuck Sicilian Villan sound. The distinct faders for the volume of your overdriven and direct signal make this pedal the perfect tool for your guitar or bass tone. This limited series' design is created by Luke Preece, a renowned artist known for his esoteric heavy metal iconography. Like all KHDK limited editions, the Totality is built entirely in our mystical Prague Custom Shop where we personally guitar-test every piece. Proudly made in the EU.
